title: Hollow Court: a beverage cellar you actually own, and HMA, the tooling that maintains it

goals.title: One repository, one application, three platforms, and the tooling beside it
goals.notes: The root of this plan. The application is offline-first with no account and no server; HMA is the maintenance toolset living under tool/, art/hma and docs/HMA*. Invariants held on every push: lib/domain and lib/data never import Flutter, the event log is append-only, and every write into the cellar goes through one path -- the model proposes, the reader confirms.

goals.title: The pure Dart domain: units, events, sync, pricing -- no Flutter import, ever
goals.notes: Volumes are microlitres, recipes are rational ratios, the event log folds into stock, and the sync format is the storage format. The suite enforces the no-Flutter rule by running on the plain Dart VM: a domain file that reached for Flutter would stop dart test from running at all.

goals.title: The data layer: append-only store, seed pipeline, chat history and settings, sealed key
goals.notes: The event store is one JSON object per line, appended and never rewritten; a torn tail is expected, not corruption. Chat history is bounded at 200 turns, the action log at 500 lines, and the chat key is sealed with AES-GCM beside the settings. **A photograph is scaled before it leaves** -- `image_compress.dart` bounds the long side at 1280 and re-encodes as JPEG on a background isolate, because a gallery original is several thousand pixels of label and the turn carrying it is re-sent on every request after it. Bytes that isolate cannot decode come back untouched, since deciding here that a file is unreadable is a decision about what a provider accepts.

goals.title: Six screens and the interaction: cellar, recipes, ingredients, journal, settings, conversation
goals.notes: The proposal cards are the write path's only door: a confirmed proposal calls applyWrite, which is the one place that names the method each write becomes. **A reply is drawn as the shapes it is made of.** `chat_render.dart` parses paragraphs, headings, lists, fenced blocks and tables, draws bold, italic and inline code instead of stripping them, and renders four charts -- line, candle, bar, pie -- with the canvas rather than a package. `chat_icons.dart` turns `:name:` into a glyph from a curated table of forty names, a character in the icon font rather than a WidgetSpan so the paragraph still lays out as one line. The transcript itself is kept whole on screen; what the model reads is trimmed in the adapter. A name or a chart body the renderer cannot use is printed as it arrived, because a visible mistake is better than a word that disappears.

goals.title: The outward seams: chat, web search, cellar tools, barcode, update check -- declared and switched
goals.notes: Barcode and chatModel start switched on; priceComparison remains an unimplemented declaration. The seven proposal kinds map to seven distinct writes through writeFor, a value-level mapping that a test reads back; the model can propose, never write.

goals.title: Three platforms from one commit: three APKs, a Windows installer and one portable archive -- and one command to install each
goals.notes: build_all.sh builds the three targets in parallel worktrees, then assembles the portable archive from their outputs, and lands receipts and a manifest in one bundle directory -- `D:\hollow-court\dist` since 2026-11-26, when the bundle moved off E: together with the checkout. Two version walls are measured rather than assumed: the MSI needs WiX 5.x, because 7.x stops at WIX7015 asking for the paid Open Source Maintenance Fee licence; and the Linux target needs `linux/CMakeLists.txt`'s install-prefix fallback, because CMake 4 no longer sets CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX_INITIALIZED_TO_DEFAULT for this template and the install step then writes to /usr/local. The two `linux/*appimage*.sh` scripts are kept but called by nothing since 2026-11-27: they are the record of how an AppImage was built and installed, including the WSLg measurement that its menu icon is `/usr/share/pixmaps/hollow_court.png` and nothing else. **The icon pipeline covers all three platforms since 2026-11-27.** `art/render_icons.sh` installs the Android densities, `assets/icon/hollow-court.png`, the Windows `.ico` and the seven files of the macOS appiconset, each from a drawing rendered at the size it serves rather than rescaled from the largest; it skips the macOS section on a checkout with no such platform, and `magick` is told to drop PNG date chunks so two runs over one source produce one byte sequence.

goals.title: HMA: the maintenance toolset -- ten commands, art checks, and the platform's account of itself
goals.notes: HMA lives beside the application in the same repository: tool/hma.py is the dispatcher, with the agent, models, art check and art render beside it, and docs/HMA* as the manual. Its release rides the HC-Stable mirror under HMA=1.

goals.title: Elizabeth, the reader's agent in the cellar: a conversation that proposes and never writes
goals.notes: OpenAI-compatible chat over SSE with a tool loop capped at four rounds, plus a fifth trouble -- `toolLoop` -- kept apart from `refused`, because that word sends a reader to check a quota that is working. Nine tools: web search, read cellar, read recipes, read one recipe in full, work out a recipe's strength through `dosing/abv.dart` and `dosing/dilution.dart`, and the six proposals that write nothing. **What the request carries is `ChatClient.trimHistory`** -- the newest eight exchanges, cut at a user message and never inside a tool round, so a `tool_calls` message is never left without its answers; the screen and the store keep every turn. **Every failure is one of five kinds**, and `IOException` as well as `SocketException` becomes `unreachable`, because a TLS handshake and a server closing mid-stream are siblings of the failure the first version caught. The prompt bans inventing bottle facts, flattery, pretending to act, and Markdown; it is prefixed with today's date because a model has no clock, names the four chart fences, and quotes the icon names. `replyIconNames` and `chatIcons` are two lists locked together by a test, because `lib/adapters` has no Flutter dependency and cannot share the constant. The key is the reader's own, sealed on this machine.
